steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) and RNA (ribonucleic acid) are both nucleic acids but differ in five main ways:

1. Sugar:  
   • DNA’s backbone contains deoxyribose (lacks one oxygen).  
   • RNA’s backbone contains ribose (has an extra oxygen).

2. Bases:  
   • DNA uses adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C), guanine (G).  
   • RNA uses A, uracil (U) instead of T, C, and G.

3. Structure:  
   • DNA is usually double-stranded, forming a stable double helix.  
   • RNA is typically single-stranded and can fold into varied shapes.

4. Function:  
   • DNA serves as long-term genetic storage.  
   • RNA acts in information transfer (mRNA), protein synthesis (rRNA, tRNA), and regulation (siRNA, miRNA).

5. Stability & Location:  
   • DNA is more chemically stable and mainly stays in the nucleus (eukaryotes).  
   • RNA is less stable, made in the nucleus but functions throughout the cell (can leave nucleus).

Bottom line: DNA stores the blueprint; RNA reads, transports, and helps execute it.
